resposta:
Forge an empire where the only currency is the depth of a person’s agony. In this state, biological decay is forbidden by decree; instead, consciousness is suspended in an eternal loop where time expands indefinitely around the mind. Citizens live in the Silent Spire, a city constructed from obsidian and bone, where the walls hum with the sound of suppressed screams. There is no death, only the permanent maintenance of the self in a state of perpetual tension. Hope is a regulated substance available only after completing a cycle of ten years of labor. Joy is classified as contraband, treated as a virus that threatens the stability of the collective will.

The Governor does not sleep; he stands amidst towers of glass where he observes the fractures in the faces of the population. Each citizen contributes a fraction of their remaining vitality to fund the empire's immortality. To lose awareness is to lose status, and to lose control is to be exiled into the Void—a state worse than death, where no thoughts exist. Instead, the people train their minds to derive meaning solely from endurance. The Emperor rules from a throne that floats above the ground, held aloft by the shared suffering of the thousands below. His power grows exactly as long as they keep the fires burning. There is no sunrise here, only the relentless, cold glow of surveillance screens that never blink off. They are the engines of the war, the soldiers of the silence, and they will never stop running toward the edge of the cliff.
